transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-09-02 14:37 UTC | Duration: 48m | Recording id: ff-20270902-aurum-1437

Summary: Intro discovery for Aurum Insights to evaluate Redwood's self-serve API and options (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Focus on time-to-first-call, free credits for a quick playground, security/compliance gating (SOC2/KMS/SAML), and a short performance pilot to validate latency and cost.

Topics: quickstart credits, SDKs, time-to-first-call, hosted vs dedicated vs vpc/private, audit logs/KMS, SLA/uptime expectations, benchmark run scheduling.

Quick links referenced: Quickstart guide: https://redwood.ai/quickstart (shared), Security pack (SOC2/ISO): https://redwood.ai/security, Benchmark sheet placeholder: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/aurum-template

Transcript: 
[00:00] Sofia Martin (Redwood AE): Hey, hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia, AE on the platform team, with Diego from our SE team. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya Nair (CTO, Aurum): Doing well — thanks. we tried to carve out time, excited to see how fast we can get to a live call.
[00:12] Diego Ramos (Redwood SE): quick intro from me — I look after performance and deployments, happy to talk through hosted and private options and run the perf bench.
[00:19] Lena Cho (Head of ML): Great. We're evaluating a couple options because our use case touches PII and payment data, so security is heavy — but first we want a fast path for prototyping. free credits and a playground would be ideal.
[00:30] Sofia: Totally. Our PLG path is designed for that — self-serve sign up, SDKs, and we can seed an account with credits so your team can go from zero to first-call in under an hour typically. depends on network/VPN stuff of course.
[00:44] Marcus Reed (Platform): when you say under an hour, are you including the SSO bits? we use SAML into Okta and our VPC has strict egress rules so that could add time.
[00:53] Sofia: Good question — the <under an hour> is for pure API usage using API keys and SDKs. If you require SAML/SSO and private VPC peering, that adds coordination — usually a day to a week depending on your security review.
[01:10] Priya: ok, that matches expectations. For the proto we want to use hosted API with credits, then if it passes security/latency we'll look at Dedicated or Private.
[01:18] Diego: Nice pattern — hosted -> dedicated -> private is what a lot of customers do. for latency, what's your target?
[01:23] Lena: 95th percentile under 300ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens). cost is also a constraint; we want to get a sense of cost per inference at our expected volume.
[01:33] Diego: 300ms 95th is achievable on hosted depending on model selection and sequence length. we'll run a quick benchmark using your prompt set to validate. note that batching and KV caching behavior affects tail latency. sometimes transcription shows KV cash, lol — but it's KV cache.
[01:48] Marcus: haha noted. also curious about token accounting and streaming. we need partial streaming for UI responsiveness.
[01:54] Sofia: We support streaming and streaming SDKs, plus function/tool calling. For billing, tokens are counted server-side; we'll provide a cost estimate based on your sample prompt set.
[02:03] Speaker 3 (maybe automated caption): background noise removed
[02:07] Lena: on security — do you have SOC2 and key management? we'd need audit logs and customer-managed KMS ideally.
[02:15] Sofia: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO docs — we'll share the security pack. For customer-managed keys, Private deployments support KMS/HSM integrations; for hosted we have envelope encryption and managed KMS but can discuss additional options.
[02:29] Marcus: and for logs, do we get token-level traces? we need per-request tracing for debugging, and retention configurable.
[02:36] Diego: Console provides per-token cost and latency breakdowns, route/model dashboards, and tracing hooks. retention tiers are add-ons — we'll include the standard audit logs in the security pack.
[02:46] Priya: timeline — we want to have the prototype in two weeks. is that realistic?
[02:50] Sofia: For a hosted self-serve prototype using credits, yes. I'll provision credits and quickstart steps today, you could be calling in hours if no network block. For a Dedicated or VPC private pilot, that typically takes 1-4 weeks depending on procurement and network approvals.
[03:03] Lena: ok, can you walk us through what Diego will run for the initial benchmark?
[03:07] Diego: Sure — perf checklist: 1) sample prompt latency for chosen model (we'll test 3 model variants), 2) 95/99th percentile tail testing at low and medium concurrency, 3) token-cost estimate using your prompt distribution, 4) validate streaming vs batch behavior, 5) KV cache warm/cold scenarios. I'll need AWS creds or a way to run inside your account for private network runs, otherwise we do hosted-account runs with representative data.
[03:31] Marcus: Credentials — we prefer not to hand over creds. can you do a synthetic mirror run?
[03:35] Diego: Absolutely — we can run a hosted-side benchmark with your sanitized prompts and we can also run a remote runner in your account via a short-lifetime role if you want.
[03:44] Priya: On the billing/credits — how much do you typically seed for a team sprint?
[03:48] Sofia: We usually seed between 5k and 25k tokens/credits depending on scope. I'll provision 10k by default, and we can top up if needed. that should be enough to validate prototypes and run small perf tests.
[03:59] Lena: great. For the quickstart, can you drop example code in Python and Node that shows streaming and identity?
[04:06] Sofia: yes, we'll send language-specific snippets and a short sample app. also a one-click sandbox if you want to try the playground in-browser.
[04:13] Marcus: mention of one-click is good. does the sandbox expose logs? we need to see request/response pairs for debugging.
[04:18] Diego: Sandbox shows request/response and basic traces; for full token-level audit you'd use the console with higher retention tier.
[04:25] Speaker 2 (Redwood SE): "We also have a small code-runner you can embed in your CI to measure cold start and cache warmups."
[04:33] Priya: procurement concerns — standard SaaS contract or do you do enterprise SOWs for Dedicated?
[04:38] Sofia: For hosted PLG it's standard online terms; for Dedicated and Private we do enterprise contracts with SLAs and support tiers. procurement typically surfaces when you move from POC to reserved capacity.
[04:48] Lena: any variability in model family names? we have internal folks used to 'llama-style' models and some names may be slightly off in transcripts, just FYI.
[04:56] Diego: yep we index model families and provide recommended quantization/variant for throughput. for cost saving, we may recommend a quantized variant or smaller family for high-volume endpoints.
[05:06] Priya: what about routing if a region goes down? we need graceful degradation — auto-fallback options?
[05:11] Diego: Smart routing exists — policy-based routing by latency, region, and cost. plus automatic fallback to compatible model variants if capacity is constrained. we'll show the routing policy UI in the demo.
[05:22] Marcus: one item — we need to validate data residency, Europe vs US. Are region pins available in hosted?
[05:28] Sofia: Yes; you can choose region pins for hosted endpoints. For stricter residency requirements, Private or Dedicated in a given cloud region is the path.
[05:36] Priya: are there examples of customers starting on hosted and moving to Dedicated? any references we can talk to?
[05:42] Sofia: We can share anonymized case studies and references — I'll add that to the follow-up.
[05:48] Speaker (automated caption): 10 minute mark
[05:51] Lena: ok, this might be a dumb question but how is the billing shown — do we get per-endpoint breakdowns so our product folks can attribute costs?
[05:58] Diego: Yes, per-route/model breakdowns and token-level cost accounting. you can export reports and hook into cost webhooks.
[06:07] Marcus: about function calling — we have an internal toolchain expecting structured outputs; does Redwood enforce schemas or is that structured output buyer-side?
[06:15] Diego: Redwood supports structured output and function/tool calling; you can validate via schemas and the runtime will surface structured outputs as JSON. it's quite flexible.
[06:24] Priya: any friction points you've seen with teams moving from hosted to private?
[06:29] Sofia: the common bottlenecks are procurement lead time, network egress rules, and KMS key handover. planning those pieces early shortens the migration.
[06:39] Marcus: on latency again — are there suggestions for prompt engineering to reduce token usage and cost?
[06:45] Diego: Absolutely — prompt compression, instruction tuning, and caching prefixes help. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations on batching, quantization and caching profiles.
[06:55] Lena: I'd like to see the Optimize recommendations applied to our prompt set in the benchmark.
[06:59] Diego: noted — I'll include those in the perf report.
[07:03] Sofia: Quick recap and next steps? I'm going to provision the credits and send the quickstart doc after the call, Diego will propose perf checklist and slot, Lena will send prompt samples, Marcus will send network diagram, and we'll schedule a follow-up deep-dive for VPC/private decisions.
[07:18] Priya: sounds good. timeline — can we aim for the hosted prototype by 2027-09-09?
[07:23] Sofia: Yes, that aligns. we'll do credits today and try to have the prototype by the 9th. Diego, you'll schedule the bench?
[07:28] Diego: I'll send a Doodle for available slots and propose 2 runs: hosted-side first, then account-run if needed.
[07:33] Speaker 1: end of call notes

- Q: Are customer-managed KMS keys supported? A: Yes for Private deployments; hosted has envelope encryption and options to discuss.
